summary: Delayed first token for chat completions after runtime 1.4.2 + model weight patch rollout
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (BrightLearn) reported unusually long Time-To-First-Token (TTFB) on chat completions immediately after our 1.4.2 runtime rollout and an accompanying model weight patch (redwood-7b-quant-v2). Impact: interactive chat experiences stall for 2–6 seconds before any token is emitted; after first token stream resumes normally.

Impact:
- Multiple enterprise/dedicated customers observed increased latency in the first token for chat endpoints (not steady-state token throughput).
- Client-side timeouts (5s) triggered for some requests, causing degraded UX and escalations to CS.

Environment:
- Runtime version: 1.4.2 (canary → staged → prod on 2026-03-10)
- Affected models: redwood-7b-quant-v2 (weight layout change + quantization metadata update)
- Regions: us-east (primary), eu-west (partial)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a single-turn chat completion request to hosted chat endpoint pinned to redwood-7b-quant-v2 on runtime 1.4.2.
2) Observe TTFB measured by client (start of request → first token).
3) Repeat with multiple warm and cold connections, and measure kernel compilation / logs on the serving node.

Observed behavior:
- TTFB spikes to 2–6s on first token (median baseline was ~200ms).
- Subsequent tokens stream at expected rates once first token emitted.
- Logs show a 1.2–1.8s period of kernel JIT/compilation activity and occasional model weight re-layout steps on the serving node.

Expected behavior:
- TTFB remains within SLAs (<=500ms for these workloads) and no client timeouts on first token for warmed nodes.

Related artifacts/links:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rt/ttfb-summary?panelId=7 (sharp rise at 2026-03-10 11:22 UTC)
- Slack incident thread: #support (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01234567)
- Canary PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/2314
comments: 2026-03-10 11:35 UTC — Aisha Park: Customer BrightLearn reports interactive chat freezing before first token; user timeouts observed. Escalating to SRE and runtime owners.

2026-03-10 11:48 UTC — Marco Chen: Reproduced in prod using canary cluster. Observed long pre-token phase with kernel compilation messages in node logs. Opening debug session on node id: node-rt-prod-usa-13.

2026-03-10 12:15 UTC — SRE (Priya Rao): Found compilation cache miss spikes coincident with rollout. Canary cluster had cache cleared by new packaging step. Investigating packaging -> kernel selection interaction.

2026-03-10 13:02 UTC — Eng (Diego Morales): Hypothesis: model weight layout change triggered different kernel selection and forced a JIT/compile path for some GPU kernels. Also saw autoscaler creating fresh instances with empty compilation caches causing first-request stalls.
2026-03-10 14:05 UTC — Marco Chen: Rolled back runtime 1.4.2 for affected pools in us-east; TTFB returned to baseline in rollback clusters. Confirming fix with BrightLearn and additional customers.

2026-03-11 09:20 UTC — Eng (Diego Morales): Deployed hotfix v1.4.2-patch01 to avoid compilation path on first inference by pre-warming kernel caches and skipping expensive weight re-layout on serving path. Monitoring.

2026-03-12 08:45 UTC — Aisha Park: Customer BrightLearn confirmed improvement; first-token timeouts reduced and customer will validate on their traffic spike next week. Marking issue resolved and scheduling postmortem.
investigation_notes: Instrumented TTFB at ingress and on-serving nodes; delta shows server-side pre-token time is the source (not network).
Node logs show calls to kernel_compiler::compile_and_cache() taking ~1.1–1.8s for a subset of kernels after weight metadata change.
Compilation cache misses correlated with autoscaler events and nodes created after the package change; older nodes with cached kernels were not affected.
Model weight patch introduced a new weight ordering that selected a different GEMM kernel family; runtime attempted a JIT fallback when precompiled kernels were not available for that ordering.
Batching and cache warmers did not trigger for very small single-request patterns; pre-warming was required to mitigate first-request stalls.
No increase in 5xx error rate was observed; errors were primarily client timeouts (4xx category) due to TTFB exceeding client-side timeouts.
Reproduced locally by booting a fresh serving instance with empty /var/cache/serving-kernels and sending single chat requests pinned to redwood-7b-quant-v2.
Telemetry: increased cpu/gpu kernel compiler time and a spike in 'kernel_compile' metric during rollout windows (11:20–11:40 UTC).
resolution: Immediate mitigation: Rolled back runtime 1.4.2 in affected Dedicated pools (us-east) to 1.4.1 at 2026-03-10 14:00 UTC; TTFB returned to baseline on those pools.

Hotfix deployed (1.4.2-patch01) that adds: (a) pre-warm routine for kernel caches on node startup for affected models, (b) skip-on-path for weight re-layout during serving (move to background), and (c) gating to avoid JIT fallback when performance-critical flag set.
Changed default first-request batching policy: reduce autoscaling of fresh nodes for single-request patterns and ensure pre-warm runs before routing traffic.
Added rollout checklist item: any model weight layout or quantization metadata change must ship with precompiled kernel artifacts or a warmup job in the image.
Monitoring and alerts: added a dedicated TTFB alert (P1) with 3-minute burn-in window and dashboard panel for kernel_compile metric.
Follow-ups: create internal postmortem (INT-4021) and a task to automate kernel artifact generation in CI (linked PR created).
Customer communication: BrightLearn notified of root cause, mitigation, and timeline; they validated improvement and accepted the hotfix.
